headline: US Official Reports Progress at Philippine EDCA Sites
seoTitle: US Official Reports Progress at Philippine EDCA Sites
seoDescription: US Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby said the Philippines and United States had made progress developing EDCA sites over the past 18 months.
deck: US Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby said the Philippines and United States had made progress developing EDCA sites over the past 18 months.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The United States has made progress developing Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement sites in the Philippines over the past 18 months, US Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby said Thursday.
Colby said Washington was working closely with the Philippine government and anticipated further progress. He framed the work as supporting Philippine sovereignty and national interests.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: EDCA, signed in 2014, allows US forces access to designated Philippine military facilities, construction of agreed facilities and the prepositioning of equipment. It does not establish permanent US bases.
There are nine agreed EDCA locations. The four added in 2023 are Naval Base Camilo Osias in Cagayan, Camp Melchor Dela Cruz in Isabela, Lal-lo Airport in Cagayan and Balabac Island in Palawan.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: EDCA development affects alliance readiness, humanitarian-response capacity and Philippine defense planning. The sites remain within Philippine military facilities, making sovereignty, access rules and the precise scope of construction continuing matters of public interest.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for official Philippine and US disclosures identifying completed projects, funding, inspection schedules and operational arrangements at individual sites.
